newsitem.title: USA: Paging Network launches VoiceNow in Dallas.
newsitem.headline: Paging Network launches VoiceNow in Dallas.

text.p: Paging Network said Monday it launched its advanced voice paging service, VoiceNow, in the Dallas-Ft. Worth area.

The company said it expects VoiceNow's wireless narrow band PCS network to reach more than 1,700 wireless transmitter/receiver stations and to offer service in more than 50 metropolitan markets by the end of 1997.

With VoiceNow, subscribers can receive voice messages with their palm-size VoiceNow pager from any telephone. The pager's push-button operation allows the user to play the message, rewind, fast-forward, and control volume.
The company's stock was up 1/4 to 14 in afternoon trading.

PageNet said it initially will offer three price packages to Dallas-Fort Worth residents, starting at $4.95 per month, and going up to either $8.95 or $16.95, based on subscriber usage. The VoiceNow pager may be purchased for $230 or leased for about $10 per month, PageNet said.
The VoiceNow pager, manufactured by Motorola Inc, uses a standard nine-volt battery and provides up to six weeks of power. The pager stores up to three minutes of messages, the company said.
PageNet has exclusive rights to the pager device for six months as part of its joint development relationship with Motorola.
About 40 million Americans currently carry pagers, the company said. It estimated the U.S. market for voice paging at between 15 and 20 million subscribers.
